walkthrough:
**Recall the three Group 17 trends**

Think of Cl at the top, then Br, then I at the bottom. Going down the group, covalent bond strength decreases, London forces increase, and oxidising power decreases.

**Use clue 1 to place X and Y**

$X_2$ has weaker covalent bonds than $Y_2$. Weaker bonds mean larger atoms further down the group. So X is below Y in Group 17.

**Use clue 2 to place X and Z**

$X_2$ has stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces than $Z_2$. Stronger London forces mean more electrons and larger $M_r$. So X is also below Z in Group 17.

Trend rule:
$$\text{London forces: } \text{I}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{Cl}_2$$

**Use clue 3 to place Y and Z**

$Y_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $Z_2$. Oxidising power is greatest at the top of the group where atoms gain electrons most easily. So Y is above Z in Group 17.

Trend rule:
$$\text{oxidising power: } \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$$

**Combine to get the order**

X is below Y, X is below Z, and Y is above Z. That gives only one vertical order from top to bottom: Y, then Z, then X. With Cl, Br, I this must be Y is Cl, Z is Br, X is I.

options.A: X is Br, Y is Cl, Z is I. Clue 1 and clue 3 fit, but clue 2 fails because $Br_2$ has weaker London forces than $I_2$, not stronger. X must be the lowest element to have the strongest London forces.
options.B: X is Cl, Y is Br, Z is I. This puts Cl at the bottom of the three, which is backwards. $Cl_2$ has the strongest covalent bond and the weakest London forces, so it cannot have weaker bonds than $Br_2$ or stronger London forces than $I_2$.
options.C: X is I, Y is Br, Z is Cl. Clues 1 and 2 fit because I is the lowest, but clue 3 fails because $Br_2$ is a weaker oxidising agent than $Cl_2$, not stronger. Y must be above Z, not below it.
options.D: X is I, Y is Cl, Z is Br. All three clues fit: $I_2$ has weaker covalent bonds than $Cl_2$, $I_2$ has stronger London forces than $Br_2$, and $Cl_2$ is a stronger oxidising agent than $Br_2$. The top to bottom order Y, Z, X matches Cl, Br, I perfectly.
